title: Nucleophiles and electrophiles
caption: Nucleophiles (top row) have a lone pair and often a negative charge, and attack electron-poor carbon. Electrophiles (bottom row) are electron-poor: a δ+ carbon next to an electronegative atom, or a cation such as NO₂⁺, and are attacked by electron-rich species.
alt: Top row: hydroxide, ammonia, cyanide and water. Bottom row: bromomethane, methanal and the nitronium ion.
description: Nucleophiles: OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻ and H₂O, each with a lone pair to donate.
Electrophiles: bromomethane (δ+ carbon), methanal (δ+ carbonyl carbon) and NO₂⁺.
